lines.text: What if you could stop time?
Just snap your fingers, and the whole world freezes.
Minute one. Birds hang in the sky, and a car stops inches from your knee.
You stroll straight through rush hour traffic, and nobody honks.
Day one. You walk onto the pitch at a packed stadium final.
You carry the ball into the net and walk away. Eighty thousand people are about to lose their minds.
Week two. Every shop in the city is yours.
No bills. No traffic. No alarm clock.
Month six. You stand beneath a giant wave, frozen above your head.
It is the best view on Earth, and you turn to tell someone.
Year one. Nobody has answered you in a long time.
Every joke lands on the same frozen smile.
Year ten. The sun has not moved once. It is always three forty two in the afternoon.
You know every face in this city, and none of them know yours.
Year forty. You find your family, exactly where you left them, laughing at something you can't remember.
You are older than your parents now.
You sit down beside them, and snap your fingers.
To them, not one second has passed. To you, it was a lifetime.
